props.title: Live music for a Sunday brunch.
props.lede: The coffee keeps coming, a table of eight is on its second round of mimosas, and in the corner upright bass and guitar are playing The Girl from Ipanema. Restaurants, hotels and clubs book it as a standing Sunday, and families book it for the morning after a wedding, a bridal brunch, a shower or a birthday. It’s the same music either way, from a duo, a solo guitarist or a pianist.

rows.text: A standing Sunday, weekly or monthly, with the same musicians every time: upright bass and guitar, a guitarist alone, or a pianist where the dining space has a piano, on one contract for the whole run.

A post-wedding brunch at the hotel, a rented house or a family’s home, with the same duo that played the cocktail hour the day before or a guitarist alone, playing the songs from the weekend. The wedding and the brunch go on the same contract.

rows.text: A private dining space, a garden, a table of twenty at home. A guitarist or a Spanish guitarist plays under the meal, and a singer with a guitar plays the songs the guest of honor asked for. Showers have their own page, and the evening version is on private parties.
A hotel’s member event, a company’s family day, a club’s Mother’s Day seating: a pianist or a duo playing the standards while the tables turn, the daytime version of a client dinner.

props.title: Standards, bossa nova, and the songs that suit a slow morning.

props.html: The duo plays the standards and the bossa novas: Autumn Leaves, The Girl from Ipanema, All of Me, Blue Bossa, Someday My Prince Will Come, and the rest of a set built for a dining space where the coffee is the loudest thing in it. A guitarist alone plays the same set instrumentally, a Spanish guitarist plays it on nylon strings for a patio, and a singer with a guitar takes the folk and singer-songwriter end of the song list.
The jazz duo and trio page covers the format in full, and the solo guitarist, Spanish guitarist and singer and guitarist pages cover the one-musician versions.

items.q: Can a restaurant or hotel book live music for brunch every Sunday?
items.a: Yes. A standing Sunday, weekly or monthly, runs on one contract with one personal contact for the run, with the same musicians every time. Tell us the seating times and the space and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price for the run. Signet Artists books brunch musicians across Denver.

About the level of the conversation at the tables, so a table of eight talks across it and the server can take an order without leaning in. Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks, so the dining space never goes quiet.

items.q: What does a dining space need?
items.a: A corner of about 8 by 6 feet for a duo or 6 by 4 for a solo, and one outlet. Setup takes 45 minutes to an hour before doors, so it's finished before the first seating, and packing up takes 30 to 45 minutes after the last. On a patio, a covered, level and dry spot with power or a battery-powered system, and a call time for moving inside. We can send a certificate of insurance and whatever else the venue asks for.
